texts.heading: Context
texts.body: Apartment L1 began as a set of rooms that already worked on paper and not in use. The brief was short: more storage, more light, and nothing that would need explaining to a guest.

texts.heading: Approach
texts.body:
One material carries most of the plan, so the joinery, the doors and the walls read as a single surface.

Everything that could be built in was drawn at 1:5 and made by a joiner we could telephone.

texts.heading: Detail
texts.body: The details are kept few and repeated, so the rooms feel calm rather than designed.

materials.note: Four materials, chosen before the plan was finished.

Every other decision follows from the plot, the light and the budget.

projects.title: Nibiru
projects.summary: Forty metres of span carrying a roof, a lighting rig and eleven days of weather. Drawn to the millimetre the rigging crew would build to.
projects.story: Forty metres of clear span carrying a roof, a lighting rig and eleven days of weather. We drew it to the millimetre the rigging crew would build to, then stood under it while they did. The last truss went in at four in the morning and the first band played at nine.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

projects.title: Ploom Aura
projects.summary: A room built around one soft source of light, so the product is the brightest thing in it and the room is almost not there.
projects.story: One source of light, one satin skin, and a room shaped so the light has nowhere to go but back to the product. Visitors spent three minutes inside on average, which is long for a room with nothing to do in it except look.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

projects.title: Kozel Forest
projects.summary: Two hundred turned posts on a slope, set out so the gaps line up from exactly one point and from nowhere else.
projects.story: Two hundred and fourteen turned posts on a six-degree slope, set out so the gaps line up from exactly one point and from nowhere else. Find that point and the forest opens into a room. Step a metre either way and it closes again.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

projects.title: Sobranie Prism
projects.summary: Angled glass over a bar, lit from inside so the room reads as one solid from the beach and as nothing at all from behind.
projects.story: Sixty-two angled panes over an eleven-metre bar, lit from inside at 2700 kelvin. From the beach it reads as one solid block of light. From behind the bar it is not there at all, which is the only side the staff ever see it from.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

projects.title: Ploom Chamber
projects.summary: Eight square metres, one visitor at a time, and a ceiling that moves slowly enough that you only notice on the way out.
projects.story: Eight square metres, one visitor at a time. The ceiling travels two hundred and forty millimetres over ninety seconds, slowly enough that nobody notices while they are inside it. Everybody notices on the way out.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

projects.title: Coca-Cola Yard
projects.summary: A yard rather than a stand: shade, seating and a counter, built so it read as somewhere to be instead of somewhere to queue.
projects.story: Three hundred and twenty square metres, sixty per cent of it in shade, built in seven weeks. We drew a yard rather than a stand: somewhere to be, with a counter in it, instead of a counter with a queue attached to it.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

projects.title: Peroni Terrace
projects.summary: A terrace that packs into two vans and goes up in a day, detailed as though it were staying.
projects.story: It packs into two vans and goes up in a day, and it is detailed as though it were staying. That is the entire brief. Temporary is a schedule, not a standard, and the joints are where the difference shows first.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

projects.title: Cold Store
projects.summary: A working cold store dressed for one night and returned the next morning. Nothing was fixed to the building.
projects.story: A working cold store, held at four degrees, dressed for one night and returned the next morning. Nothing was fixed to the building: every element stands, leans, or hangs from what was already there. It was struck by seven and back in service by nine.
projects.approach: We drew it from the way people would arrive, stand and leave, and only then from the brand. Every element was checked against how it would be built, carried and struck, so what went up on site was the drawing and nothing else.

interior-design.name: Interior Design
interior-design.title:
Interior
Design
interior-design.text: Apartments, offices, and the rooms inside houses that were finished by somebody else. Joinery drawn at 1:5, one material asked to do the work of three, and a joiner we can telephone.
interior-design.stripLine: Six interiors, drawn at 1:5 and made by a joiner we can telephone.

architecture.name: Architecture
architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.text: Houses, extensions and the odd building that refuses to be either. We take the plot, the light and the budget as the three fixed facts and let every other decision follow from those.
architecture.stripLine: Eleven built since 2016, and the ground each of them stands on.

real-estate-marketing.name: Real Estate Marketing
real-estate-marketing.title:
Real Estate
Marketing
real-estate-marketing.text: A development sells on an image of a building nobody can walk into yet. We draw that image out of the same model the thing will be built from, so what a buyer is promised and what gets poured are the same thing.
real-estate-marketing.stripLine: What a building looks like a year before anyone can walk into it.
